capturedWith: Google Chrome 156.0.8078.47, headless (--headless=new), driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol from a Node script with a throwaway user-data-dir. Each element was read only after the Angular app had rendered it. The only interactions were clicking the filters toggle, the modal close button and the desktop Hide button.

pageTitles.search: Search ClinicalTrials.gov for: asthma | Card Results | ClinicalTrials.gov

viewportsTested: plus a width sweep from 390 to 1400 at a height of 900
consentOrCookieBanner: No cookie or consent wall appeared and nothing blocked rendering. The page shows the standard section.usa-banner government banner and a div.usa-alert.usa-alert--warning disclaimer. Neither was interacted with.

filtersBreakpoint.evidence: Fresh page loads at 1023 and 1024 pixels, a downward resize sweep from 1400 to 390 and an upward resize sweep from 390 to 1280 all switched at exactly the same place. At 1024 pixels and wider the page renders ctg-focus-your-search-panel (a sidebar with a Hide or Show button). At 1023 pixels and narrower that panel is not in the DOM and ctg-focus-your-search-mobile-modal renders a Focus Your Search button that opens a modal. 768x1024 behaves exactly like 390x844. The home page has no such switch: its form is rendered inline at 390, 768 and 1400 pixels.

desktop.ariaExpanded: The button has no aria-expanded attribute.
desktop.ariaControls: The button has no aria-controls attribute.
desktop.accessibleNameSource: Its text content, which is "Hide" when the panel is expanded and "Show" when it is collapsed. The icon is an svg with aria-hidden="true".
desktop.behavior: Clicking Hide removes the filters panel content and the Clear Filters and Apply Filters footer from the DOM, so ctg-checkbox-tree-filter#adv-check-status, ctg-checkbox-tree-filter#adv-check-studyType, input#advcond and input#location-input are all absent until Show is clicked. The panel div.filters-panel loses its expanded class. The panel is expanded by default.

narrow.id: The button has no id while the modal is closed. After it is opened, the modal library assigns a random id of the form modal-123456, so never select by id.
narrow.ariaExpanded: The button has no aria-expanded attribute in either state.
narrow.accessibleNameSource: Its content: an img with alt="Focus Your Search" followed by the text "Focus Your Search (1)". The number in parentheses is the count of active filters and is absent when no filters are active, so match the prefix "Focus Your Search".
narrow.modalWrapper: div#focus-your-search-modal.usa-modal-wrapper with role="dialog", aria-labelledby="modal-1-heading" (no element with that id exists) and aria-describedby="modal-1-description". It is a direct child of body. Class is-hidden means closed and class is-visible means open. After opening, the wrapper gets data-opener set to the toggle button id.
narrow.modalCloseButton: button.usa-modal__close with aria-label="Close button for Narrow your search" and data-close-modal=""
narrow.modalFooterButtons: Clear Filters: button.usa-button.secondary-button.clear-btn. Apply Filters: button.usa-button.primary-button, which carried the disabled attribute in the captured state, where no filter had been changed. On the desktop panel these two buttons have ids clear-filters and apply-filters, but the modal copies have no ids.
narrow.statusAndTypeGroupsWhenClosed: Both groups are still in the DOM while the modal is closed, but they are not rendered (the modal wrapper has visibility hidden), so a visibility check fails until the toggle is clicked. Inside the opened modal the More Filters accordion is already expanded, so Study Type is visible without a second click.

differencesFromUserSuppliedStatusMarkup: The user-supplied description matches the live DOM: a div.filter-group contains legend.group-title "Study Status" and ctg-checkbox-tree-filter#adv-check-status, and the Recruiting checkbox has id adv-check0-status1 and value rec. The exact original markup text was not available to this capture, so a character-level diff could not be made. Details that the live DOM adds are these: every element carries Angular _ngcontent-ng-c and _nghost-ng-c attributes and many empty comment nodes; every label has a trailing span.agg-count with the live count, so the label text is "Recruiting (374)" for this query; the group contains a second legend ("Expanded access", class font-body-md) with a collapsed sub-accordion of four more checkboxes; and the checkbox inputs are visually hidden off screen by USWDS styling.

fixtureCleaning: Only script, style and noscript elements, the d attribute of svg path elements, and inline base64 data were removed, and a one-sentence HTML comment was added at the top of each file. No script, style, noscript or base64 content was present inside the captured elements, so nothing else changed. Angular scoped attributes and empty comment nodes were deliberately left in place.
proseNotes: On /search the filters are a sidebar at 1024 pixels and wider and a "Focus Your Search" modal at 1023 pixels and narrower. The sidebar has a Hide or Show button that adds and removes the whole filter content from the DOM. The modal keeps its content in the DOM at all times and only toggles the is-hidden and is-visible classes on div#focus-your-search-modal, so a guided walkthrough must click button[aria-controls="focus-your-search-modal"] first and then wait for the wrapper to have is-visible before highlighting the Recruiting or Interventional labels. The home page has no collapsing panel, but its Study Type group stays hidden until the More Filters button is clicked, and its status control is a pair of radios rather than checkboxes.
